summary: Russian missile attacks on Kyiv resulted in 14 deaths and 60 injuries, with significant damage in Podilskyy and Darnytskyi districts. Drone activity persisted across multiple regions including Chernihivshchyna, Kharkivshchyna, and Odeschchyna. Air raid alerts remained active with reports of cruise missiles and drones targeting infrastructure.
key_points: Russian missile attack on Kyiv killed 14 people and injured 60, damaging buildings in Podilskyy and Darnytskyi districts. (Source: @UkraineNow/82443)
Drone groups moved through Chernihivshchyna toward Brovary and Kyivshchyna, with additional drones reported near Kharkiv and Sumy. (Source: @kpszsu/67500)
Crimea experienced a total blackout after satellite imagery showed fires at power stations and airfields including Sevastopol and Kerch. (Source: @UkraineNow/82442)
Air raid alerts warned of cruise missiles over Kyiv and explosions in the capital region, with 600 people evacuated from Vishnevyi. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68603)
Russian forces conducted airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia fuel stations, injuring five including a woman and 11-year-old child. (Source: @UkraineNow/82446)
Ukrainian air defenses shot down 4 drone groups over Kyiv, with no Iskander-M or Tsirkon missiles intercepted overnight. (Source: @eRadarrua/99927)
President Zelenskyy reported Russian preparation for a new mass attack, urging citizens to heed air raid signals. (Source: @UkraineNow/82434)
Darnytskyi district strike destroyed part of a building, killing 6 residents and rescuing 28 including two 4-year-olds. (Source: @UkraineNow/82443)

sections.executive_summary: Russian missile strikes on Kyiv killed 14 civilians and wounded 60, with significant infrastructure damage and evacuations in Vishnevyi. Drone activity intensified across northern and eastern regions, targeting energy infrastructure in Crimea and military sites in Kharkiv and Odesa. Air raid alerts remained active with reports of cruise missiles and multiple drone groups approaching from various directions.
ukraine: Missile attack on Kyiv killed 14 people and injured 60, with building damage in Podilskyy and Darnytskyi districts. Evacuation of 600 people occurred in Vishnevyi due to fire risks from struck facilities. (Source: @UkraineNow/82443)

Air raid alerts warned of incoming cruise missiles over Kyiv, with explosions reported in the capital region. Two children aged 4 and 11-month-old were among the injured in Vishnevyi strike. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/68603)

Russian airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia fuel stations injured five people including an 11-year-old boy and his mother. Evacuations continued in areas affected by air pollution from attacks. (Source: @UkraineNow/82446)

President Zelenskyy stated Russia is preparing a new mass attack, urging citizens to follow air raid signals. Air quality deteriorated in Kyiv due to smoke from missile strikes. (Source: @UkraineNow/82434)

Ukrainian air defenses tracked multiple drone groups moving from Chernihivshchyna toward Kyiv and Brovary. No Iskander-M or Tsirkon missiles were intercepted overnight despite active engagement. (Source: @eRadarrua/99927)
russia: Russian Ministry of Defense claimed mass strikes on Kyiv and surrounding regions targeting Ukrainian military infrastructure. TASS reported the attacks were in response to Ukrainian terrorism. (Source: @tass_agency/383972)
Russian forces conducted airstrikes on Zaporizhzhia fuel stations, causing injuries and infrastructure damage. Attacks extended to energy facilities in occupied Crimea. (Source: @UkraineNow/82446)
Army Group North advanced in Sumy direction, engaging in battles near Bachevsk, Pisarevka, and Novaya Sech. Liberated villages included Losevka in Kharkiv direction. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31405)

Russian propaganda claimed destruction of Ukrainian UAVs and secondary detonations from strikes. Fighter jets scrambled from Poland in response to long-range aviation activity. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31405)

Russian government allocated over 3 billion rubles for industrial mortgage programs and increased non-resource exports by 11%. Manufacturing growth reached nearly 23% over five years. (Source: @tass_agency/383966)
eastern_front: Army Group North conducted offensive operations in Sumy direction, fighting in Shostka, Krasnopollye, and forest areas. Assault troops advanced in Kharkiv direction near Kazachaya Lopan. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31405)

Russian forces liberated the village of Losevka after driving out Ukrainian Territorial Defense Brigade units. Battles continued in Petro-Ivanovka and forest areas near Budarky. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31405)
Drone activity reported near Kharkiv from the south and in Odesa from the Black Sea. UAVs moved toward Zaporizhzhia and Dnipro from southern directions. (Source: @kpszsu/67512)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian forces maintained high-intensity missile and drone campaigns targeting urban centers and infrastructure across Ukraine. The use of cruise missiles and drones resulted in significant civilian casualties, particularly in Kyiv where 14 people were killed. Attacks on energy infrastructure in Crimea caused widespread blackouts, disrupting essential services. Air defense systems successfully intercepted multiple drone groups, though cruise missiles penetrated defenses. The threat of additional mass attacks remains elevated, especially following President Zelenskyy's warnings of impending Russian operations.
sections.regional_response: Polish fighter jets scrambled in response to Russian long-range aviation activity, indicating regional escalation. European NATO countries and Canada committed €70 billion in military aid for Ukraine over 2026-2027, with Germany as the largest contributor. Ukrainian air defenses actively engaged incoming threats, shooting down 4 drone groups over Kyiv. Civilian evacuations and emergency response measures were implemented in affected regions, including Vishnevyi and Kyiv areas. International monitoring of the conflict continued through various channels and diplomatic communications.
sections.intelligence_notes: Drone activity patterns suggest coordinated attacks from multiple directions, with groups moving through Chernihivshchyna toward Kyiv and from southern regions targeting Odesa and Zaporizhzhia. Russian forces demonstrated capability to target energy infrastructure in occupied territories, causing strategic disruption. Air defense performance varied, with successful drone interception but cruise missile penetration. Civilian impact assessments indicate significant collateral damage in urban areas, with ongoing evacuation and emergency response operations. Intelligence sources report preparation for additional mass attacks, suggesting sustained Russian offensive operations.
